notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware backend was run or added. The package serves the first confirmed entry symbol, HopperURDFEnvV3 (my_pybullet_envs/hopper_env_v3.py:32), through GymnasiumDriver. The upstream is an old-style gym.Env (reset() without a seed, a four-tuple step and a separate seed()); the Gymnasium bridge handles that legacy API itself, so the card's family-config decision and helper were kept (no deviation). Only the fake backend is declared. NOT COVERED: the other three card entry symbols (HopperCombinedEnv, LaikagoBulletEnvV4, LaikagoCombinedEnv; listed in facts.md), the real PyBullet environment, and the sim backend (gym.make); pybullet and gym==0.14.0 are not installed where the gate runs, and the fake was not compared with upstream. The fake is a pure-Python kinematic stand-in, so the fidelity contract claims F0 with engine custom:simgan-hopper-kinematic, not the upstream F1 rigid-body simulation; the start positions, thresholds and other test-data constants in fake.py are marked # placeholder, the 11-value observation array is fully represented (no omitted array), and the registration max_episode_steps=500 is a gym.make wrapper that neither the fake nor the bridge enforces. Expected warnings only: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the bridge only records the seed for the next reset) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the integer/numeric inputs the bridge derives; there are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. Only catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used, so there are no catalogue requests. gate.digest is the digest line the check printed (the report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run.
